description: An elderly man with a gold-trimmed cap, coral-bead necklaces and a patterned wrap kneels in a dim earthen workshop, pouring glowing molten metal from a small crucible held in tongs into a rough clay mould. On a shelf behind him stand gold-coloured cast heads and small figures; a charcoal furnace, pots and tools surround him and a second worker tends a fire at left. No letters, border or frame; a small sparkle logo sits cropped in the bottom-right corner.
reason: Shows a traditional West African bronze caster pouring molten metal into a clay mould in a pre-industrial workshop, but the card is the 1954 Georgetown-IBM machine translation demonstration in New York. Nothing in the picture is a computer, IBM machine, office or 1950s setting; this looks like art for a different (metalworking) card.
